subtitle: Supported decision-making helps a person understand options and communicate their own choice. Learn how to offer that help without taking the decision over.
scope: For staff across DHS learning the basics of supported decision-making through an original personal-choice fiction. The course distinguishes chosen assistance from substituted decisions, pressure and assumed legal authority. It does not assess capacity, draft a legal agreement, change a guardianship order, approve a purchase or determine service eligibility. Actual legal, program, service, access and protection responsibilities remain with the responsible people. Learning is voluntary. Private reflection and supplied example are valid; no actual personal, financial or service records are required. Native American and Tribal-specific matters are referred to the appropriate office within ADSA.
introTranscript: People often use help to understand a decision. Supported decision-making keeps that assistance connected to the person’s own choice. This course follows Milo’s practice comparison of two phone arrangements. You will examine the chosen help, the information and tradeoffs, different learned meanings of advice, and the difference between communicating a choice and replacing it. You will also recognize why a support conversation does not establish legal authority or a guaranteed outcome. Learn at your own pace; no actual purchase or public reflection is required.

lessons.title: Keep the person as the decision maker
lessons.summary: Distinguish assistance with a choice from another person choosing the answer.
lessons.objective: Explain supported decision-making as chosen help with understanding and communicating a decision.

Identify Milo’s purpose and the assistance actually requested.
Distinguish help from a substituted choice or a capacity conclusion.

lessons.statement: Help with the decision is different from deciding for the person.

image.caption: Three people stand outside a building; two shake hands.

intro.heading: Listen for the decision and the wanted help
intro.body:
Supported decision-making begins with the person and the particular choice. Minnesota’s definition describes assistance from people the individual chooses to help them understand potential personal and financial decisions and, when consistent with their wishes, communicate a decision. The assistance is meant to enable the person’s decision, not turn every helper into someone with control over the person’s life.

In the example, Milo wants a replacement phone for calls and messages with friends. Two arrangements are described: a phone bought separately with a monthly service charge, and a phone bundled with a longer service agreement. Milo asks Inez to help compare the charges and asks Kai to join a discussion because Kai has experience using one of the devices. Milo has not asked either person to choose the arrangement, sign a contract or contact a seller on Milo’s behalf. The case does not establish a diagnosis, guardianship or legal restriction.

Inez can help organize the information. Kai can describe the actual experience with the device. Neither form of assistance decides whether the price, features and obligations fit Milo’s priorities. Milo’s request for help also does not establish inability to choose. People may seek assistance because the terms are unfamiliar, the calculation is inconvenient or another perspective helps them notice something. Do not complete a capacity finding from the presence of a supporter.

A proposed note says, “Milo needed help, so Inez selected the best plan.” The first part does not justify the second. The useful distinction is between understanding information and choosing among the arrangements. Ask what Milo wants the assistance to accomplish and preserve any actual limits on the requested involvement. The person may want help for this comparison without wanting a helper in every future financial or personal decision.

Supported decision-making is also different from simply leaving the person alone with confusing terms. Retaining agency can include wanted assistance. Actual legal or service requirements need their responsible process if relevant; this example does not approve a contract, determine capacity or replace any real decision-making authority. Privately consider a decision for which you wanted another person’s experience or explanation while keeping the final preference your own. You may use Milo’s example without disclosing a personal purchase, asking someone to evaluate you or producing a live work product.

accordion.heading: Distinguish the parts of Milo’s request

items.title: Compare is not select
items.body: Milo asked Inez to help compare charges. An accurate table can make the differences easier to consider. Choosing the answer instead would add a role that was not requested and could obscure what Milo values.

items.title: Experience is not authority
items.body: Kai can say how a device worked in their experience. That information may be useful, but does not establish what Milo should purchase or a legal right to sign for Milo. A familiar product and a trusted relationship remain different from authority.

items.title: Assistance is not inability
items.body: The example describes a question and requested help, not a capacity evaluation. If a formal concern requires a particular process, responsible people use that process. The classroom must not manufacture a diagnosis or legal conclusion from the fact that Milo wants a comparison.

tabs.heading: Compare three responses to the request

tabs.label: Take over
tabs.body: “Inez will choose because Milo asked for help” replaces the requested comparison with someone else’s answer. It may feel efficient, but the phone’s purpose and the actual preference can disappear. A help request does not itself authorize a substitute decision.

tabs.label: Leave alone
tabs.body: “Milo must read every term without help to prove independence” turns agency into an unnecessary test. The person asked for assistance, and using it can be part of their own decision. Respecting choice does not require refusing a useful explanation.

tabs.label: Support the choice
tabs.body: Inez can organize the supplied charges and Kai can describe their experience, while Milo considers the options. That fits the requested roles and leaves unresolved information visible. It does not establish that the contract is approved or that every formal requirement has been met.

check.correct: Help compare the arrangements and describe relevant experience while preserving Milo’s own choice.
wrong: Select the answer because asking for help proves inability.
Refuse all assistance so Milo must prove independence.
Treat Kai’s product experience as authority to sign a contract.
check.feedbackCorrect: The response supports the stated decision and keeps assistance, preference and authority separate.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Asking for help does not establish inability or a transfer of choice. Refusing all assistance ignores the actual request and turns independence into a test. Product experience does not give signing authority. Each tempting shortcut replaces one part of Milo’s request with an unsupported conclusion.

lessons.title: Clarify the chosen help
lessons.summary: Make the role and limits of each supporter understandable without assuming that trust gives unlimited permission.
lessons.objective: Identify the different assistance roles Milo requested from Inez and Kai.
objectives: Identify the different assistance roles Milo requested from Inez and Kai.
Distinguish a chosen supporter from an automatically authorized representative.
Choose a way to address an offered helper’s interests and information sharing without inventing a legal finding.
takeaways: The person’s choice of help can be specific to a decision or part of a task.
Trust does not automatically establish every permission or legal authority.
A helper’s interest in the outcome should be made visible rather than hidden in the advice.
lessons.statement: Ask what the person wants each supporter to help with.

image.caption: Three people stand outside a building; two shake hands.

intro.heading: Define help in ordinary words
intro.body:
A supported decision can involve more than one person, with different kinds of assistance. It is useful to clarify those roles in ordinary language. “Help me compare the monthly charges” is different from “Help me explain my choice to the seller.” A person may want both, one or neither. A supportive relationship should not silently expand into every part of the decision or every future matter.

Milo wants Inez’s help with the amounts and Kai’s experience with features. The example adds that Milo wants to discuss the options first without contacting a seller. That limit matters. Inez can organize the figures and Kai can explain which features they actually use, but an immediate call placing an order would move beyond the involvement Milo requested. A person can welcome advice while retaining a preference about when and how others become involved.

A third person offers to help. The person works for the seller of the bundled option and may benefit from a sale. Their product information might still be useful if accurate, but that interest should not be hidden or treated as neutral control of the comparison. The case does not establish fraud or a legal conflict determination. It gives a reason to distinguish sales information from the role of a chosen independent supporter and to ask what involvement Milo actually wants.

Information sharing also needs care. Wanting help with two charges is not automatically permission for a helper to send every personal, financial or service record to another reader. Ask what information is needed for the requested assistance and use the actual consent, privacy and authority requirements that apply. Do not promise absolute confidentiality or assume a relationship creates the authority to access, disclose or sign anything. The course does not supply those legal permissions.

The support roles may change. Milo can ask Kai to pause, want a different explanation or seek another person’s perspective. That is not automatically ingratitude, inability or failure of the approach. If a legal arrangement or actual program requirement affects the situation, its scope needs the responsible process rather than a class vote. No one in this example is appointed to a guardianship or financial role by being helpful.

Privately reflect on the difference between wanting advice and wanting someone to act for you. You may use the supplied roles without describing your own relationships or finances. The useful result is a clearer account of requested help, limits and interests, not a required support agreement, a legal finding or a list of real people who must now take responsibility for a purchase.

lessons.keyStatement: A trusted person’s helpfulness does not establish every authority or disclosure permission.

flashcards.back: The particular assistance the person wants from someone, such as explanation or communication.
A stated boundary on involvement, such as discussing options before contacting a seller.
A benefit or concern that may shape advice and should not be hidden in the comparison.
The consent or authority that applies to access, communication or action; it cannot be assumed from helpfulness alone.

items.title: Amounts and features differ
items.body: Inez’s figures and Kai’s experience answer different questions. Keeping those contributions distinct helps Milo use both without accepting either as the whole answer. A helper can be valuable without being made responsible for every task.

items.title: Do not skip the person’s timing
items.body: Contacting the seller before Milo wants that step changes the discussion into an action. Respect the requested pause while keeping actual obligations in view. A quick order may look efficient but would not fit the involvement supplied in this case.

items.title: Show an interest without guessing motive
items.body: A seller’s employee may benefit from the bundled sale. Naming that supplied interest allows Milo to consider the information appropriately. It does not justify an unsupported accusation or mean every product statement is false; examine accuracy and the chosen support role separately.

tabs.heading: Compare trusted help and assumed control

tabs.label: Chosen assistance
tabs.body: Inez helps with the figures because Milo asked, while Kai describes actual use of the device. The roles remain specific and can be clarified as the discussion continues. This arrangement supports the choice without creating a legal appointment or an obligation to accept the advice.

tabs.label: Relationship as permission
tabs.body: “Kai is a friend, so they can share all records and place the order” adds powers the example does not tell us. The friendship may explain trust, but it does not establish every consent or authority. Unnecessary sharing and premature action can occur when those parts are silently combined.

tabs.label: Hidden interest
tabs.body: Treating the seller’s employee as a neutral decision maker can conceal why a recommendation favors one option. Make the interest visible and examine accurate information with Milo. Do not replace that inquiry with either automatic acceptance or an accusation that the case cannot substantiate.

check.question: What best fits the roles and limits supplied?
check.correct: Keep the requested comparison roles, respect Milo’s pause on seller contact, and make the seller’s interest visible.
wrong: Let Kai order immediately because friendship establishes authority.
Send every financial record to the seller because help was requested.
Treat the seller’s interest as proof that every statement is fraudulent.
check.feedbackCorrect: This preserves chosen assistance, the actual timing and the relevant interest without inventing powers or findings.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Friendship does not establish ordering authority. A limited help request is not blanket permission to disclose every record. The seller’s interest warrants a clear comparison, not a fraud finding without evidence. Each shortcut replaces a specific question with an unsupported permission or accusation.

lessons.title: Explain the options and consequences
lessons.summary: Make relevant facts understandable without hiding costs, commitments or missing information.
lessons.objective: Calculate the supplied twelve-month base charges for the two practice arrangements.
objectives: Calculate the supplied twelve-month base charges for the two practice arrangements.
Distinguish an equal base total from an identical commitment or a complete actual bill.
Choose a comparison that answers Milo’s purpose and preserves unresolved information.
takeaways: Relevant comparisons explain effects as well as totals.
Equal base charges do not make all terms or experiences identical.
Missing fees, coverage or conditions should remain visible rather than assumed.
lessons.statement: A useful comparison explains what the numbers include and what they leave open.

image.caption: Three people stand outside a building; two shake hands.

intro.heading: Compare the facts Milo wants to use
intro.body:
Supporting a decision can include turning unfamiliar terms into a clear comparison. The helper should preserve meaning rather than simplify away the obligations. An easy-to-read answer that hides a cost or assumption may be less useful than an honest explanation of what still needs checking. The person’s actual purpose determines which differences deserve attention.

The example supplies these figures solely for practice. Arrangement A has a one-time phone price of $120 and a base service charge of $15 per month. Arrangement B has no initial phone charge and a base service charge of $25 per month with a twelve-month minimum service commitment. The supplied charges do not include taxes, additional fees, service coverage, early-ending conditions or what happens to a device after an agreement ends. The account does not establish actual eligibility for either arrangement or the ability to pay.

Using only those figures, twelve months of A is $120 plus twelve times $15, or $300. Twelve months of B is twelve times $25, also $300. This calculation compares the supplied base amounts over the same period. It does not mean every bill will be equal, that either arrangement is best, or that their commitments are interchangeable. In particular, an initial payment and a stated minimum commitment affect the decision differently even when the base total matches.

Milo asks, “What happens if I want to stop after six months?” The example does not tell us a complete answer. A helper should not invent a cancellation policy from the lower monthly figure, assume an early fee or guarantee a refund. Identify the relevant term for verification through the appropriate information holder. Similarly, calls and messages depend on actual service and device suitability; a price comparison cannot establish that all wanted functions will work.

A useful account therefore says what the calculation includes, compares the initial payment and supplied commitment, and records Milo’s unresolved question. It can use a table, an oral explanation or another wanted form of communication, with actual access requirements where relevant. The goal is understanding, not recitation of a financial script or agreement with a helper’s preference. This classroom calculation is not financial advice, a benefits determination, a legal interpretation of a contract or permission to place an order.

Privately examine how an attractive phrase such as “free phone” could draw your attention away from an ongoing commitment, or how a single total could obscure differences you value. You may consider the supplied amounts without entering your own income, accounts or purchase history. A clearer question can be a useful result even when the correct next step is to obtain information rather than complete the decision.

lessons.keyStatement: Equal base totals do not establish equal terms, complete bills or the right choice.

flashcards.back: A calculation using the supplied charges and period, with exclusions stated rather than hidden.
An obligation or condition of an arrangement that needs accurate examination alongside price.
A condition not supplied, such as early ending, which must not be invented from a familiar label.
A difference that affects the person’s actual purpose or decision, not just the helper’s preferred measure.

items.title: Use the same period
items.body: Comparing one initial payment with one monthly charge would not answer the twelve-month question. The same period makes the arithmetic interpretable. Still, the result covers only the supplied charges; do not turn it into a promise about a complete actual bill.

items.title: An initial payment changes the timing
items.body: A’s $120 initial phone amount may matter to Milo differently from monthly amounts. The example does not tell us Milo’s resources. A helper can explain the timing without assuming affordability or selecting an arrangement for the person.

items.title: An unanswered term remains open
items.body: Milo’s six-month question concerns conditions the case does not provide. State that clearly and identify what needs verification. Guessing an early fee or assuring there is none would create a more confident answer at the cost of accuracy.

tabs.heading: Compare three ways to explain the figures

tabs.label: The free label
tabs.body: “B is free because the phone has no initial charge” leaves the monthly service and minimum commitment out of the explanation. The phrase can appear simple while changing the meaning. Milo needs the ongoing charge and actual conditions to be part of the comparison.

tabs.label: The same-total label
tabs.body: “Both are $300, so they are identical” correctly notices the supplied twelve-month base arithmetic but incorrectly extends it to timing, commitment, coverage and missing terms. Keep the useful calculation without erasing the remaining choice.

tabs.label: A relevant comparison
tabs.body: Explain the base total, initial payment, stated commitment and the unanswered early-ending question. This gives Milo information to weigh while making the limits visible. It does not select the product, determine affordability or turn a practice table into an approved contract.

check.question: What is accurate about the supplied twelve-month comparison?
check.correct: Both base totals are $300, but payment timing, the stated commitment and missing terms still matter.
wrong: B has no cost because its phone has no initial charge.
The equal base totals prove every term and actual bill are identical.
The calculation establishes Milo can afford either arrangement and should order now.
check.feedbackCorrect: The answer retains the actual arithmetic and its limits, leaving the person’s choice and missing information open.
check.feedbackIncorrect: The free label omits twelve monthly charges. Equal base amounts do not establish all terms, fees or coverage. The figures contain no evidence of Milo’s resources and do not authorize an order. Each shortcut turns a useful piece of information into a broader conclusion it cannot support.

move.control: You explain both the relevant figures and what they do not establish.

lessons.title: Understand the meaning of advice
lessons.summary: Recognize different learned expectations about consultation while keeping the person’s choice open.
lessons.objective: Explain Inez’s and Kai’s different learned meanings of receiving advice.
objectives: Explain Inez’s and Kai’s different learned meanings of receiving advice.
Distinguish understanding an account from requiring agreement or rejecting all help.
Choose a response that reflects Milo’s stated preference without predicting an identity group’s behavior.
takeaways: Advice and the response to it can carry different learned meanings.
Consulting another person does not automatically require choosing their answer.
Wider understanding can change the response without diagnosing or ranking anyone.
lessons.statement: Understand what consultation means before treating a different choice as disrespect.

image.caption: Three people stand outside a building; two shake hands.

intro.heading: Examine the expectation behind the advice
intro.body:
Supporters can agree on the value of choice yet interpret the consultation differently. One person may hear asking for advice as inviting a carefully considered recommendation; another may hear it as seeking ideas while preserving a separate final voice. The question is not which person has the better identity or development level. It is how their individually learned meanings shape the exchange and what the person actually wants.

Inez explains a learned experience from a family cooking group. People discussed menu choices together, and a recommendation from someone who had examined the ingredients was taken seriously as care for the shared meal. Considering that advice visibly helped maintain a relationship of mutual responsibility. Inez learned to hear an immediate rejection after requesting help as a sign that the person’s effort had not been valued. Inez initially interprets Milo’s wish to think further as dismissing the comparison work.

Kai explains a different experience from a student newspaper. Editors offered detailed criticisms, but the writer retained a recognizable voice and sometimes declined a suggestion with an explanation. Kai learned to hear separate consideration after advice as responsible authorship, rather than rejection of the editor. Kai initially interprets Inez’s desire for a quick response as an attempt to replace Milo’s decision. These are two supplied personal accounts, not rules about families, writers, age or identity groups.

When the meanings are understood, Inez can recognize that a pause or different choice may preserve authorship rather than express disregard. Kai can recognize that advice can carry an invitation to mutual consideration rather than a demand for control. Neither understanding determines Milo’s preference. The example supplies Milo’s statement: “I want your views, and I want time to consider them. I may choose something different.”

They can respond by presenting the comparison and relevant experience as contributions, leaving room for Milo to consider them and ask further questions. Inez does not need a forced agreement to show the effort mattered, and Kai does not need to withdraw all help to preserve choice. A specific acknowledgment such as “the comparison helped me notice the commitment” can be offered if it fits Milo’s wishes, but it is not a gratitude requirement or a condition for receiving assistance.

This response adapts because the learned meanings and actual account mattered. It does not assign an intercultural orientation, diagnose motives or erase formal requirements. The personal insight can be valuable even if no purchase follows. Privately consider a learned expectation about advice, consideration or separate judgment. You may keep that reflection unrecorded or use the example without disclosing personal relationships. Understanding your own expectation can broaden the next interaction without a public proof of learning.

lessons.keyStatement: A different choice can coexist with valuing the help that informed it.

flashcards.back: What an individual has learned to hear in asking for and receiving advice, examined through their account.
Keeping the person’s own voice in the decision rather than requiring a helper’s answer.

accordion.heading: Understand both accounts without completing Milo’s meaning

items.title: Consideration can express care
items.body: Inez’s cooking-group account helps Kai understand why advice feels relational rather than merely informational. Taking that meaning seriously does not require Milo to choose Inez’s answer. The response can acknowledge the contribution while leaving the actual decision open.

items.title: A pause can express responsibility
items.body: Kai’s newspaper account makes separate judgment understandable as authorship rather than dismissal. Inez can reconsider the first interpretation without treating every quick decision as inauthentic or requiring all people to follow a writer’s process.

items.title: The person supplies the preference
items.body: Milo explicitly wants views and time, with room to choose differently. That account provides direction beyond the supporters’ disagreement. If the account had not been supplied, they would need to ask rather than predict a preference from Milo’s identity or from their own learning.

tabs.label: Require agreement
tabs.body: Inez could insist that asking for advice obligates Milo to accept the preferred arrangement. This would make one learned meaning control the outcome. A careful contribution can matter without the person being required to turn it into their final choice.

tabs.label: Reject all help
tabs.body: Kai could say that retaining authorship means declining every explanation. That would replace Inez’s imposed answer with a different universal rule. Milo has asked for assistance, and the comparison can support authorship instead of canceling it.

tabs.label: Understand and adapt
tabs.body: They can explain their meanings, reconsider the first interpretations and provide wanted assistance with time for Milo’s own consideration. The practical response changes because the accounts mattered. It does not establish a personal assessment result, universal rule or obligation to disclose a private reflection.

check.question: Which response best reflects the wider understanding?
check.correct: Provide the wanted comparison and experience, with time for Milo’s own choice and no agreement or gratitude condition.
wrong: Require Milo to accept Inez’s answer because the advice took effort.
Remove every offer of help so the choice can be authentic.
Rank the supporters’ intercultural orientations from their conversation.
check.feedbackCorrect: The response uses the different meanings and Milo’s account without replacing choice, withholding help or claiming an assessment.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Effort does not make the recommendation compulsory. Authentic choice can include wanted assistance; removing all help ignores the request. The conversation does not establish personal orientation ranks. Each shortcut treats one surface sign as the whole meaning and misses the actual learning or choice.

items.text: Inez learned that visibly considering advice expressed mutual responsibility.

lessons.transfer: Privately consider how your learned meaning of advice affects your first interpretation of another response.

move.control: You can value a contribution while preserving the person’s separate choice.
move.failure: A personal expectation becomes compulsory agreement, universal advice rejection or a rank.

image.caption: Three people stand outside a building; two shake hands.

intro.heading: Keep speaking assistance and signing authority distinct
intro.body:
Supported decision-making can include help communicating a decision when that assistance fits the person’s wishes. Communication is not automatically authorization to make a purchase, share unrelated information or sign a legal document. A useful support account distinguishes what the person wants conveyed, who will convey it and what the next action actually is.

Milo now asks Inez to help put the early-ending question into ordinary words for the seller. Milo wants the question answered before deciding and does not want an order placed. Inez can help formulate the question and communicate it in a way consistent with Milo’s wishes and applicable requirements. Reporting that request as “Milo authorized the bundled purchase” would change an inquiry into a commitment the person did not make.

If Milo later wants help communicating a chosen arrangement, confirm the actual preference and requested role. Do not assume that all conversation partners have authority to sign, that a familiar supporter can act whenever Milo pauses, or that a brief course table is a legal agreement. Actual consumer, financial, privacy and program requirements may apply, depending on the situation; the course does not interpret every contract or authorize an actual transaction.

Formal decision-making arrangements require a separate and accurate account. Minnesota’s guardianship law assigns the court particular findings concerning incapacity and less restrictive means; the court grants only the powers necessitated by the person’s demonstrated limitations and needs. The bill of rights preserves rights not restricted by court order. A helper, relative or class participant cannot infer the contents of an order from a diagnosis or family relationship, appoint themselves or erase an existing order by renaming a discussion supported decision-making.

The relevant distinction is between using assistance as an approach and determining a particular legal arrangement. A written description of chosen help may be useful in some circumstances, and an actual process may require documents. Its existence or absence does not let the course decide a legal outcome. Responsible legal and program roles must examine the actual situation, with the person’s participation and rights preserved. This lesson is not instructions to petition a court, diagnose capacity or bypass an appointed role.

For staff, the practical skill is to avoid silently adding authority while making an explanation clearer. Say that the person requested a question, not a purchase; that a formal matter is pending, not resolved by a worksheet; or that a role has not been established, not supplied by a relationship. Actual current access, service, safety and protection responsibilities remain separate from optional learning and should not wait for a course discussion. Privately practice with the practice question without sending a real seller message, signing an agreement or sharing someone’s records.

inThisLesson: Actual requirements without classroom legal findings.
lessons.keyStatement: A clearer message must preserve the actual decision and authority rather than add a commitment.

flashcards.back: Assistance expressing a question or decision in a way consistent with the person’s wishes.
The specific step the person wants, such as asking a question, distinguished from an order or signature.
The actual rights and powers established through the legal process, not inferred from a label or relationship.
Using assistance to understand a decision is different from determining a specific legal document, order or role.

items.title: A question is not an order
items.body: Milo asks about ending the arrangement before deciding. The message should preserve that sequence. A seller-facing summary that says the option was selected could create confusion or pressure even though it is shorter and sounds decisive.

items.title: A supporter is not every representative
items.body: Inez’s chosen communication help does not itself supply signing power for every document. Examine the actual role and required process for an actual action. Neither confidence nor a close relationship substitutes for the relevant authority.

items.title: A label cannot change an order
items.body: Calling an exchange supported decision-making cannot dissolve an existing guardianship or create new powers. The actual order, responsible process and retained rights matter. The course introduces that distinction without deciding an individual’s legal status or prescribing a court outcome.

tabs.label: Question
tabs.body: “Milo wants to know the conditions for ending after six months before deciding” keeps the actual inquiry and timing. It gives the seller a specific issue to answer without reporting a purchase. The person’s preference and other relevant terms remain open.

tabs.label: Added purchase
tabs.body: “Milo chose B; place the order” would add a decision the example does not supply. That change is substantive, not just a shorter way to explain the question. Helpful communication needs to preserve the distinction so another reader does not act on an invented commitment.

tabs.label: Assumed authority
tabs.body: “Inez can sign everything because the discussion was supportive” makes the label do legal work it cannot establish. Actual role, scope and requirements need the responsible process. Retaining the person’s voice does not require ignoring a valid existing order or inventing one.

check.question: What should Inez help communicate at this point?
check.correct: Milo’s early-ending question before deciding, without placing an order or assuming additional authority.
wrong: An immediate purchase of B because communication help was requested.
A finding that the worksheet dissolved any possible legal arrangement.
A universal right for every trusted supporter to sign all documents.
check.feedbackCorrect: The response preserves the actual question, wishes and role, leaving purchase and formal authority separate.
check.feedbackIncorrect: The purchase adds a preference Milo has not supplied. A worksheet cannot dissolve an actual court order or decide a legal status. Trust does not establish universal signing powers. Each answer expands the communication request into a different action or authority without the required basis.

sorting.heading: Distinguish wishes, actual formal process and overreach

items.text: Milo wants the early-ending question answered before deciding.
Milo does not want an order placed now.
The actual scope of any relevant court order must be examined.
Authority to sign a real document must be established.
The supportive label dissolves every existing order.
The friend relationship appoints a universal legal representative.

lessons.next: Review the useful assistance and what the case still leaves unanswered.

scenario.context: Fiction: a summary turns Milo’s seller question into an order and describes the worksheet as universal signing authority.
scenario.prompt: Which revision best preserves the role?
options: Keep the summary because certainty helps the seller.
State the actual question and no-order limit; actual signing or legal roles need their proper process.
Replace all communication with a diagnosis of inability.
responses: Certainty does not justify changing a question into a purchase or inventing powers.
This corrects both the communication and authority without making an individual legal finding.
The case contains no assessment basis for that conclusion and communication help need not be removed.

lessons.transfer: Privately notice when a concise summary changes a question into a decision or action.

move.control: You keep the person’s actual message and the responsible action role distinct.
move.failure: A helpful label or relationship supplies a legal power or commitment that was never established.
move.next: If useful, write the practice seller question accurately. Do not send a real message, sign an agreement or use this activity to postpone an actual required response.

lessons.title: Review what the support made clearer
lessons.summary: Describe useful understanding and unresolved matters without scoring a person or claiming a legal outcome.
lessons.objective: Describe Milo’s supplied learning and remaining question without inventing a purchase or legal result.
objectives: Describe Milo’s supplied learning and remaining question without inventing a purchase or legal result.
Distinguish a changed support preference from a failure or obligation to show gratitude.
Choose a follow-up account that preserves evidence, the person’s voice and actual responsibilities.
takeaways: A useful comparison can be a result even when the decision is still open.
A person can revise the kind of help they want without failing the approach.
Course completion is not a capacity, contract, guardianship or lasting-effectiveness finding.
lessons.statement: An accurate review can value understanding while leaving the next decision open.

image.caption: Three people stand outside a building; two shake hands.

intro.heading: Keep the progress and the unanswered matters together
intro.body:
A supported-decision-making review should not measure success only by whether the person chose the helper’s recommendation or completed a transaction. Useful assistance might make a term understandable, help someone ask a question, identify an unwanted involvement or preserve their own voice. The review should also make unanswered matters visible rather than claiming a complete outcome from limited information.

The example supplies Milo’s final account: “The table helped me see that the base totals match over twelve months, but the timing and commitment differ. I want the early-ending answer before I choose.” No purchase has been made. Actual fees, coverage and contract conditions remain unconfirmed. This is a useful account of clearer understanding and a specific next question. It is not evidence that either arrangement is affordable, that every term is understood or that a formal legal question has been resolved.

Milo also says they want Inez to keep helping with the charges but do not need Kai at the next discussion. Kai’s experience was useful, yet the next task concerns a different question. That preference should not be labeled ingratitude or proof that supported decision-making failed. The person’s chosen help can be specific and revisable, while actual roles and duties remain. If the requested assistance is unavailable, name that limitation rather than pretending the person has a network they do not have.

Inez and Kai can recognize their personal learning about advice, consideration and authorship. Inez no longer needs a quick agreement to interpret the comparison as valued; Kai no longer treats every wanted recommendation as loss of voice. Those insights do not establish a personal orientation rank, diagnostic finding or permanent guarantee about future interactions. They can remain private and useful without a public declaration or a purchase as proof.

A follow-up through the actual appropriate role can seek the unresolved term and check what Milo wants next. If another formal process is relevant, keep it explicit rather than claiming the support table solved it. Minnesota’s current report describes varied forms of assistance and formal arrangements; its reported program experiences are not a promise that a particular person will avoid, remove or reduce guardianship simply by completing an exercise. An individual legal outcome needs its actual basis and responsible process.

Privately consider what a truthful short account would preserve: Milo’s purpose, wanted roles, useful information, unanswered terms and next choice. Avoid turning “not yet selected” into inability or “helpful table” into universal success. The course supports understanding and judgment within your role; it does not require an actual order, private records, public gratitude, a legal agreement or live work product to complete learning.

inThisLesson: An honest account without personal or legal scoring.
lessons.keyStatement: An open decision can coexist with useful understanding and a clear next question.

flashcards.back: What the person says became clearer, recorded without expanding it into every possible outcome.
A preference not yet selected; that status alone does not establish inability or failure.
A changed preference about help that can reflect the next task rather than rejection of the person who helped.
An account that keeps purpose, actual events, the person’s voice and unanswered matters visible.

accordion.heading: Value the result without exaggerating it

items.title: The table answered part of the question
items.body: Milo describes a clearer distinction between equal base totals and different commitments. Preserve that understanding without saying every fee or term is settled. A partial explanation can be useful while another question still needs an answer.

items.title: The next helper can differ
items.body: Milo wants Inez’s help with the charges and no longer needs Kai’s device account at the next discussion. That is specific to the next task. Do not turn it into a gratitude demand or an inability label; the person’s requested help still matters.

items.title: Formal outcomes remain separate
items.body: No contract, capacity or court result is supplied. The review should not infer one from a clear comparison or a completed worksheet. If an actual formal matter needs attention, use its responsible process while continuing to respect the person’s participation and retained rights.

tabs.label: Transaction score
tabs.body: “No purchase means support failed” ignores the useful comparison and the person’s unresolved question. It can pressure Milo to choose before the relevant term is known. The outcome to describe is understanding and the wanted next step, not a transaction demanded by the course.

tabs.label: Universal success
tabs.body: “The table proved capacity and eliminated every formal restriction” gives the learning activity powers and evidence it does not have. Useful information is not a legal finding. The actual situation and responsible process must determine any formal outcome.

tabs.label: Accurate progress
tabs.body: “Milo found the base comparison useful, wants the early-ending answer and has not chosen an arrangement” preserves both progress and limits. It supports an appropriate next inquiry while leaving the person’s choice theirs. No identity profile, orientation rank or guaranteed effect is added.

check.question: Which final account best fits the supplied information?
check.correct: Milo found the comparison useful, wants a missing term answered and has not chosen an arrangement; actual formal matters remain separate.
wrong: No purchase proves supported decision-making failed.
The table established every legal authority and permanently proved capacity.
Kai must remain involved and receive public gratitude for the assistance to count.
check.feedbackCorrect: The account preserves useful understanding, the person’s next question and the limits without forcing a transaction or legal conclusion.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A pending choice does not erase learning. A table cannot establish every legal power, capacity finding or future effect. A helper’s contribution does not create compulsory future involvement or public gratitude. Each shortcut measures a different unsupported outcome rather than the actual purpose and account.

sorting.heading: Keep progress, questions and overclaims separate

items.text: Milo says the base-charge comparison was useful.
Milo wants Inez rather than Kai at the next charge discussion.
The early-ending conditions have not been supplied.
Actual fees and coverage still need verification.
The worksheet proved permanent capacity and changed a court order.
The absence of a purchase proves the person failed.

lessons.next: Keep the job aid for private reflection or an actual appropriate inquiry within your role.

scenario.context: Fiction: Milo has a clearer comparison and an unanswered term, but no purchase. The report calls that failure and demands a public thank-you.
options: Require a purchase so the course has a measurable result.
Keep the gratitude condition because help created an obligation.
Describe the useful understanding, unanswered question and chosen next help without a purchase or gratitude gate.
responses: The course must not turn the transaction into a prerequisite for understanding or agency.
A contribution does not require public disclosure or acceptance of a helper’s desired outcome.
This keeps the actual evidence and person’s voice visible without inventing failure or authority.

lessons.transfer: Privately notice what changed in your understanding of advice, agency or useful assistance.

move.control: You describe progress and limits without turning a choice into a person’s score.
move.failure: A pending decision, changed helper or partial understanding becomes failure or universal certification.
move.next: If useful, privately review the example or write a short practice account. No actual purchase, agreement, public reflection or private records are required.

jobAid.title: Support the decision without taking it over
jobAid.subtitle: Keep the person, the chosen help and the actual authority visible.
jobAid.intro: Use Milo’s an example or reflect privately. This aid is not a capacity assessment, contract, legal agreement, eligibility decision or change to a court order.

sections.heading: Ask what help is wanted
items: Identify the person’s purpose and the particular decision rather than assuming a diagnosis or a need for control.
Ask who the person wants involved, what help they want and what information can appropriately be shared.
Do not make family membership, professional confidence or an offered worksheet proof of legal authority.

sections.heading: Explain options and preserve choice
items: Compare relevant facts, consequences and missing information in a form the person can use.
Distinguish another person’s advice from the person’s actual preference. Chosen consultation does not automatically transfer the decision.
Notice whether your learned meaning of helpful advice creates pressure to agree or a demand to reject all assistance.

sections.heading: Communicate and review accurately
items: Help communicate a decision only in a way consistent with the person’s wishes and actual requirements.
Confirm actual legal and program roles through the responsible process; a classroom support plan cannot change an existing court order.
Keep what occurred, what the person found useful and what remains unknown separate from universal success or legal conclusions.

remember: The person’s chosen assistance is not the same as a substitute decision maker.
Understanding and communicating are distinct parts of support.
A trusted relationship does not establish every authority or permission to share information.
Private personal learning need not produce a public reflection or actual purchase.
Native American and Tribal-specific matters are referred to the appropriate office within ADSA.

sources.title: Minnesota law: guardianship findings and order

sources.title: Minnesota law: retained rights and preferences
